cards.explanation: The answer is that it gets trampled and eaten by birds. The seed falls along the path, where it was trampled, and the birds of the air devoured it. I think that seed barely had time to look around. It's a rough ending, and Jesus doesn't dress it up.

The answer is moisture. The seedlings withered because they had no moisture. They did come up first, but the moisture was missing. A dough with no liquid in it does the same thing, friends. It just crumbles.

The answer is True. The seed falls among thorns, and the thorns grow up with it and choke the seedlings. They weren't just nearby, friends, they grew up right alongside. Imagine trying to stretch out with a crowd of thorns in the same pot. I'd have no room for my mustache.

The answer is a hundredfold, friends! The seed on good soil sprang up and produced a crop, and Jesus says it's a hundredfold. One seed turning into a hundred. If my dough did that, I'd need a bigger planet.

The answer is that they ask what the parable means. His disciples asked Him what the parable meant. They went straight to the One who told it. I think that's the smartest move anybody makes in this whole scene.

The answer is False. Jesus tells His disciples, “The knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of God has been given to you…” Given, friends, not kept back. Then He explains the parable to them, and says the seed is the word of God.

The answer is the devil. Jesus says the devil comes and takes away the word from their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved. He names the one who does it, friends. That's a serious line, and Jesus says it plainly.

The answer is root. Jesus says the rocky-ground people hear the word and receive it with joy, but they have no root. They believe for a season, then fall away in the time of testing. Joy on top, friends, and nothing holding it down below.

The answer is False. Jesus says the rocky-ground people believe for a season, but in the time of testing, they fall away. The joy was real at the start, and the root was what was missing. It's a sober line, friends, and I'll leave it sober.

The answer is True. Jesus says those among the thorns are choked by the worries, riches, and pleasures of this life. That's three things, friends, and not one of them sounds like a villain. Ordinary stuff can be the very thing that chokes them, and Jesus says their fruit does not mature.

The answer is that they cling to it and persevere. Jesus says the good-soil people hear the word, cling to it, and by persevering produce a crop. Hearing is the start, friends, and holding on is the next part. Think of it like a good dough you keep working until it's ready.

The answer is True. Jesus says the person who lights a lamp sets it on a stand, so those who enter can see the light. A lamp's whole job is to be seen by the people walking in, friends. Nobody lights one just to hide it.

The answer is that they will all be brought to light. Jesus says, “…there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed, and nothing concealed that will not be made known and brought to light.” Nothing is left out of that sentence, friends. It's said twice, in two different ways.
The answer is how they listen. Jesus says, “Pay attention, therefore, to how you listen.” Not only what you hear, friends, but how you hear it. That's a good one to take with you out of the bakery.

The answer is taken away. Jesus says, “…whoever does not have, even what he thinks he has will be taken away from him.” It's a sobering line, friends, and it comes right after He tells them to pay attention to how they listen. I think He wants every one of us to take that seriously.
